meta.title: SLATE research: health visits, providers, prices, waits, pharmacy and referrals
meta.method: WebSearch result summaries plus WebFetch where sites allowed it. Many publisher pages (citizensinformation.ie, beckershospitalreview.com, goodrx.com, vch.ca) returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so the figure was taken from the search engine's summary of that page; those carry verification 'search-summary'. Figures read from a fetched page carry verification 'fetched'. Nothing here is invented; where nothing was found the value is null with a note.

verificationLevels.fetched: Read directly from the cited page by WebFetch.
verificationLevels.search-summary: Taken from the search engine's summary of the cited page; the page itself was not opened. Treat as likely-correct, re-check before shipping as a hard figure.
verificationLevels.estimate: A published range or typical figure, not a fixed tariff. Must be shown as an estimate in-game.

referrals.rule: Member chooses a primary care physician (PCP). A written referral from the PCP is usually required before seeing a specialist; without it the plan may not pay. Out-of-network care generally not covered except emergencies.
No referral needed; member can see any provider in or out of network, paying more out of network.

Specialist (consultant) care normally requires referral by the registered GP or a hospital doctor (NHS e-Referral Service). Self-referral exists for some services: talking therapies, sexual health, stop-smoking, some maternity/antenatal and drug-and-alcohol services; A&E needs no referral. You cannot self-refer to a hospital specialist.

A GP referral is required to see a consultant. As a public patient, outpatient consultant care is free but you do not choose the consultant and waiting lists apply. As a private patient you pay the consultant (private health insurance may cover). GP referral also removes the EUR 100 ED charge.

Specialist visits are paid by OHIP as a consultation only with a referral from a physician or nurse practitioner; a visit without a referral cannot be billed as a consultation and many specialists will not see the patient. Self-paid specialist visits reported at roughly CAD 150-300+.

Publicly funded specialist visits require a referral from a family doctor or nurse practitioner; without it MSP will not cover the appointment. EDs need no referral. Once accepted, a referral no longer expires (BC scrapped the six-month re-referral rule).

Affiliates are assigned to a Unidad de Medicina Familiar (first level). The family doctor refers to second-level specialty care (Hospital General de Zona) with the referral/counter-referral form 4-30-8; the specialist returns the patient via counter-referral. Urgencias needs no referral. Reported wait from referral to first specialty consult ~61 days (see waits).
No referral needed to see a private specialist; patient pays directly (Simiclínicas specialist consults reported over MXN 1,000).
